520	/// Copy `[stub_start, stub_end)` into `frame` (resolved via HHDM) and
521	/// flush the I-cache so the upcoming EL0 fetch sees the new bytes.
522	///
523	/// SAFETY: `frame` must be exclusively owned (not yet mapped anywhere)
524	/// and the HHDM mapping for its PA must be live. `stub_start..stub_end`
525	/// must be a valid byte range in the kernel image.
526	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
527	unsafe fn copy_stub_into_frame(frame: Frame, stub_start: *const u8, stub_end: *const u8) {
528	    // SAFETY: end >= start by linker layout; offset_from is well-defined
529	    // on a single rodata symbol pair.
530	    let len = unsafe { stub_end.offset_from(stub_start) } as usize;
531	    assert!(len > 0 && len <= PAGE_SIZE);
532	    // SAFETY: caller's invariants hold; we have the sole pointer to this
533	    // frame, and HHDM is the only mapping.
534	    unsafe {
535	        let dst = phys_to_hhdm(frame.addr());
536	        core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(stub_start, dst, len);
537	        flush_icache_range(dst as u64, len);
538	    }
539	}
540	
541	/// Write all per-stub fields into `p`. Extends slice 2.5's helper with
542	/// `ttbr0_pa` and `asid` — the rest mirrors slice 2.6.
543	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
544	// Per-stub slot fields are independent scalars; a struct would not clarify them.
545	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
546	fn populate_stub_slot(
547	    p: &mut Proc,
548	    nr: ProcNr,
549	    priv_id: Option<PrivId>,
550	    id: u8,
551	    entry_va: u64,
552	    stack_top: u64,
553	    ttbr0_pa: u64,
554	    asid: u8,
555	    heap_window: HeapWindow,
556	    frozen: bool,
557	) {
558	    // Name: `id` followed by "-stub\0..." padding. Lets the clock tick
559	    // handler print `name[0]` to identify which stub is running.
560	    p.name = [0; 16];
561	    p.name[0] = id;
562	    p.name[1] = b'-';
563	    p.name[2] = b's';
564	    p.name[3] = b't';
565	    p.name[4] = b'u';
566	    p.name[5] = b'b';
567	
568	    p.nr = nr;
569	    p.endpoint = boot_endpoint(nr);
570	    p.priv_id = priv_id;
571	    p.priority = crate::proc::table::SRV_Q;
572	    // 5 ticks per quantum = 50 ms at 100 Hz.
573	    p.quantum_ms = 5;
574	    p.quantum_left = p.quantum_ms as u64;
575	
576	    // EL0 entry state.
577	    p.regs.elr_el1 = entry_va;
578	    p.regs.sp_el0 = stack_top;
579	    p.regs.spsr_el1 = STUB_SPSR_EL0;
580	
581	    // Per-proc address space. Stored on the slot; the scheduler reads
582	    // both on every EL1 → EL0 transition.
583	    p.ttbr0_pa = ttbr0_pa;
584	    p.asid = asid;
585	
586	    // Kernel-resolved heap window (slice 3.2). Empty for A/B/C.
587	    p.page_fault_state = crate::proc::PageFaultState::EMPTY;
588	    p.heap_window = heap_window;
589	
590	    // Run-queue link starts cleared — `sched::enqueue` sets it.
591	    p.next_ready = None;
592	
593	    // Mark runnable — or, for a frozen stub (E), leave it blocked awaiting a
594	    // privilege: RTS_NO_PRIV is the same "built but not yet privileged" state
595	    // a forked child will hold in 4.6, cleared by `SYS_PRIVCTL`. The address
596	    // space above is fully built either way, so `schedule_next`'s
597	    // ttbr0/asid asserts hold whenever the proc first becomes runnable.
598	    let rts = if frozen { RTS_NO_PRIV } else { 0 };
599	    p.rts_flags.store(rts, Ordering::Relaxed);
600	}
601	
602	/// Install priv slots for A, B, C. Unchanged from slice 2.6.
603	///
604	/// SAFETY: single-threaded boot; touches priv-table slots 16, 17, 18
605	/// sequentially.
606	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
607	unsafe fn install_stub_privs() {
608	    // SAFETY: sequential mutable borrow.
609	    unsafe {
610	        install_one_stub_priv(STUB_A_PRIV_ID, STUB_A_PROC_NR, STUB_B_PRIV_ID);
611	    }
612	    // SAFETY: A's borrow has been dropped.
613	    unsafe {
614	        install_one_stub_priv(STUB_B_PRIV_ID, STUB_B_PROC_NR, STUB_A_PRIV_ID);
615	    }
616	    // SAFETY: B's borrow has been dropped.
617	    unsafe {
618	        install_stub_c_priv();
619	    }
620	    // SAFETY: C's borrow has been dropped.
621	    unsafe {
622	        install_stub_d_priv();
623	    }
624	}
625	
626	/// Install stub C's priv slot. Differs from the A/B helper: trap_mask =
627	/// USR_T (SENDREC only), ipc_to opened just to SYSTEM, k_call_mask
628	/// opened just to `SYS_GETINFO`.
629	///
630	/// SAFETY: single-threaded boot; mutates only priv-table slot
631	/// `STUB_C_PRIV_ID`.
632	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
633	unsafe fn install_stub_c_priv() {
634	    let system_priv_id = {
635	        // SAFETY: read-only snapshot; no live `&mut Proc` here.
636	        let table = unsafe { proc_table_ref() };
637	        let idx = proc_index(SYSTEM).expect("SYSTEM in proc table");
638	        table[idx]
639	            .priv_id
640	            .expect("SYSTEM priv populated by proc::init")
641	    };
642	
643	    // SAFETY: priv index in-range; no overlapping reference held.
644	    let pr: &mut Priv =
645	        unsafe { priv_slot_mut(STUB_C_PRIV_ID).expect("stub C priv slot in range") };
646	    pr.id = STUB_C_PRIV_ID;
647	    pr.proc_nr = Some(STUB_C_PROC_NR);
648	    pr.flags = SYS_PROC | BILLABLE | PREEMPTIBLE;
649	    pr.trap_mask = USR_T;
650	    pr.ipc_to.fill(0);
651	    set_sys_bit(&mut pr.ipc_to, system_priv_id);
652	    pr.k_call_mask.fill(0);
653	    set_call_bit(&mut pr.k_call_mask, (SYS_GETINFO - KERNEL_CALL) as usize);
654	    pr.notify_pending.fill(0);
655	    pr.asyn_pending.fill(0);
656	    pr.sig_mgr = boot_endpoint(RS_PROC_NR);
657	}
658	
659	/// Install stub D's priv slot (slice 3.5/3.6). D drives `brk` and, since slice
660	/// 3.6, `mmap`/`munmap`: it issues `VM_BRK` / `VM_MMAP` / `VM_MUNMAP` SENDRECs to
661	/// the VM server, then touches the regions it created. All three ride the same
662	/// D→VM edge, so D gets `trap_mask = USR_T` (SENDREC only, like stub C) with
663	/// `ipc_to` opened to VM's priv slot and nothing else. `k_call_mask` stays
664	/// empty — D never calls the kernel directly; it talks to VM, and its page
665	/// faults reach VM via the kernel (`mini_pf_send`, which performs no permission
666	/// check).
667	///
668	/// VM's own `ipc_to` was filled by `init_boot_image` only for the active boot
669	/// priv slots `[0, n_active)` (≈ 0..15); stub D's slot is 19, so VM cannot
670	/// reply to D's SENDREC out of the box. This helper also opens that reverse
671	/// direction (VM → D) as a separate, sequential priv-slot borrow.
672	///
673	/// SAFETY: single-threaded boot; mutates priv-table slots `STUB_D_PRIV_ID`
674	/// and VM's slot, one mutable borrow at a time.
675	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
676	unsafe fn install_stub_d_priv() {
677	    // Resolve VM's priv id from a read-only snapshot (mirrors stub C resolving
678	    // SYSTEM). No live `&mut Proc`/`&mut Priv` is held here.
679	    let vm_priv_id = {
680	        let table = unsafe { proc_table_ref() };
681	        let idx = proc_index(VM_PROC_NR).expect("VM in proc table");
682	        table[idx].priv_id.expect("VM priv populated by proc::init")
683	    };
684	
685	    // Stub D's own priv slot: SENDREC to VM, nothing else.
686	    // SAFETY: priv index in-range; no overlapping reference held.
687	    {
688	        let pr: &mut Priv =
689	            unsafe { priv_slot_mut(STUB_D_PRIV_ID).expect("stub D priv slot in range") };
690	        pr.id = STUB_D_PRIV_ID;
691	        pr.proc_nr = Some(STUB_D_PROC_NR);
692	        pr.flags = SYS_PROC | BILLABLE | PREEMPTIBLE;
693	        pr.trap_mask = USR_T;
694	        pr.ipc_to.fill(0);
695	        set_sys_bit(&mut pr.ipc_to, vm_priv_id);
696	        pr.k_call_mask.fill(0);
697	        pr.notify_pending.fill(0);
698	        pr.asyn_pending.fill(0);
699	        pr.sig_mgr = boot_endpoint(RS_PROC_NR);
700	    }
701	
702	    // Open VM → D so VM can reply to D's SENDREC. Separate borrow: D's `&mut
703	    // Priv` above has been dropped.
704	    // SAFETY: priv index in-range; no overlapping reference held.
705	    {
706	        let vm_pr: &mut Priv = unsafe { priv_slot_mut(vm_priv_id).expect("VM priv slot in range") };
707	        set_sys_bit(&mut vm_pr.ipc_to, STUB_D_PRIV_ID);
708	    }
709	}
710	
711	/// Set the per-stub priv slot. `peer_priv_id` is the only target the
712	/// stub is permitted to send/notify (encoded as a single bit in
713	/// `ipc_to`).
714	///
715	/// SAFETY: single-threaded boot; mutates only the priv slot at `id`.
716	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
717	unsafe fn install_one_stub_priv(id: PrivId, owner: ProcNr, peer_priv_id: PrivId) {
718	    // SAFETY: priv index in-range; no overlapping reference held.
719	    let pr: &mut Priv = unsafe { priv_slot_mut(id).expect("stub priv slot in range") };
720	    pr.id = id;
721	    pr.proc_nr = Some(owner);
722	    pr.flags = SYS_PROC | BILLABLE | PREEMPTIBLE;
723	    pr.trap_mask = SRV_T;
724	    pr.ipc_to.fill(0);
725	    set_sys_bit(&mut pr.ipc_to, peer_priv_id);
726	    pr.k_call_mask.fill(0);
727	    pr.notify_pending.fill(0);
728	    pr.asyn_pending.fill(0);
729	    pr.sig_mgr = boot_endpoint(RS_PROC_NR);
730	}
731	
732	/// Print one line per stub showing its `(ttbr0_pa, asid)`. Run once at
733	/// the end of `userland_bootstrap`; proves each stub has a distinct
734	/// per-proc address space.
735	///
736	/// SAFETY: single-threaded boot; read-only borrows on proc slots 11..=14.
737	#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]
738	unsafe fn print_addrspace_summary() {
739	    use crate::arch::aarch64::uart::Pl011;
740	    use core::fmt::Write;
741	    let mut uart = Pl011::new();
742	    let _ = writeln!(uart);
743	    for &nr in &[
744	        STUB_A_PROC_NR,
745	        STUB_B_PROC_NR,
746	        STUB_C_PROC_NR,
747	        STUB_D_PROC_NR,
748	    ] {
749	        // SAFETY: sequential read-only borrow of the slot; no other
750	        // reference held while we read.
751	        let p = unsafe { proc_slot_mut(nr).expect("stub slot in range") };
752	        let _ = writeln!(
753	            uart,
754	            "[as] stub {} nr={} ttbr0_pa={:#x} asid={}",
755	            p.name[0] as char,
756	            p.nr.get(),
757	            p.ttbr0_pa,
758	            p.asid,
759	        );
760	    }
761	}

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! Kernel-call numbers — the `m_type` values for `SENDREC`s addressed to the
4	//! `SYSTEM` task.
5	//!
6	//! Numbering convention follows MINIX 3 `include/minix/com.h` (`KERNEL_CALL`
7	//! base, contiguous offsets). Only the 14 calls needed by Phase 2 are
8	//! defined; more are added as later phases come online.
9	
10	/// Base for kernel-call numbers. Matches MINIX 3 `KERNEL_CALL`.
11	pub const KERNEL_CALL: i32 = 0x600;
12	
13	#[allow(clippy::identity_op)] // explicit `+ 0` keeps the table aligned visually
14	pub const SYS_GETINFO: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 0;
15	pub const SYS_PRIVCTL: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 1;
16	pub const SYS_FORK: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 2;
17	/// PM → kernel: replace a target proc's program image (slice 4.7). Target
18	/// endpoint in payload `0..4` (i32); the boot-embedded binary name (NUL-padded,
19	/// `EXEC_NAME_LEN` bytes) in `4..4+EXEC_NAME_LEN`. The kernel resolves the name
20	/// in the MXBI archive (`BootImage::module_by_name`), builds a fresh address
21	/// space, resets the target to the new entry point, and tears down the old AS.
22	/// Target-taking (like `SYS_FORK`). On success the target is resumed at the new
23	/// image with no reply; failures return a negative errno to PM.
24	pub const SYS_EXEC: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 3;
25	pub const SYS_EXIT: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 4;
26	/// Raw privileged cross-address-space copy (MINIX 3 `sys_datacopy`), real as of
27	/// slice 5.2. Payload: source endpoint in `0..4` (i32, `SELF` allowed),
28	/// destination endpoint in `4..8` (i32), source address in `16..24` (u64),
29	/// destination address in `24..32` (u64), byte count in `32..40` (u64).
30	/// No grant is involved and there is no per-target authorization — the
31	/// `k_call_mask` gate is the whole check, the `SYS_VMCTL` trust stance. Used
32	/// for small control-plane reads (e.g. VFS fetching a caller's path string).
33	pub const SYS_COPY: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 5;
34	/// Grant-mediated cross-address-space copy, real as of slice 5.2. One call
35	/// number covers both directions via the selector in payload `0..4`
36	/// ([`SAFECOPY_FROM`] / [`SAFECOPY_TO`]). Payload: direction in `0..4` (i32),
37	/// granter endpoint in `4..8` (i32), grant id in `8..12` (i32), offset within
38	/// the granted range in `16..24` (u64), the *caller's* buffer address in
39	/// `24..32` (u64), and the byte count in `32..40` (u64). The kernel reads the
40	/// grant entry out of the granter's own address space and validates kind,
41	/// access, grantee, sequence, and range before copying.
42	pub const SYS_SAFECOPY: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 6;
43	pub const SYS_IRQCTL: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 7;
44	pub const SYS_VMCTL: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 8;
45	pub const SYS_SCHEDULE: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 9;
46	pub const SYS_SETALARM: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 10;
47	pub const SYS_TIMES: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 11;
48	/// Server → kernel: the servers' debug channel (slice 5.1). Subcode in payload
49	/// `0..4` (i32); for `DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG`, the text length in `4..8` (i32) and
50	/// the text itself inline in `DIAG_TEXT_OFF..DIAG_TEXT_OFF+len`. The kernel
51	/// prints one console line per call, prefixed with the *caller's own* name as
52	/// the kernel knows it. Caller-local. MINIX 3 (`kernel/system/do_diagctl.c`)
53	/// passes a `(buf, len)` user pointer here; minix.rs carries the text inline
54	/// so the debug channel needs no user-copy machinery and cannot fault — it has
55	/// to work while the copy engine and grants are themselves under construction.
56	pub const SYS_DIAGCTL: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 12;
57	/// Server → kernel: register the caller's grant table (slice 5.2). Payload:
58	/// entry count in `4..8` (i32; 0 clears the registration) and the table's base
59	/// address *in the caller's own address space* in `16..24` (u64). The kernel
60	/// records `(addr, entries)` in the caller's `Priv` and reads entries back out
61	/// of that address space on each `SYS_SAFECOPY`, so the granter pays no kernel
62	/// memory and may revoke unilaterally. Caller-local in effect, but it mutates
63	/// the caller's privilege slot, so it is routed with the target-taking calls.
64	/// A process on a *shared* privilege slot is rejected (`EPERM`): one table
65	/// address cannot describe several processes' memory.
66	pub const SYS_SETGRANT: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 13;
67	/// Scheduler claim/release. A user-space scheduler (SCHED) calls this to take a
68	/// target proc under its management (`target.scheduler = caller`) or hand it
69	/// back to the kernel scheduler (`SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL`). Made real in slice 4.3
70	/// alongside `SYS_SCHEDULE`; payload layout mirrors `SYS_VMCTL` (flags in
71	/// `0..4`, target endpoint in `4..8`).
72	pub const SYS_SCHEDCTL: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 14;
73	/// Raise a signal on a target proc (slice 4.5). Target endpoint in payload
74	/// `0..4` (i32), signal number in `4..8` (i32, `1..NSIG`). The kernel records
75	/// the signal in the target's pending bitmap (`cause_sig`) and notifies PM,
76	/// which drains via `SYS_GETKSIG` / `SYS_ENDKSIG`. This is the MINIX 3
77	/// non-PM-caller semantics (queue toward PM); PM's own direct-delivery branch
78	/// (`send_sig` to a system proc) is deferred until a consumer exists.
79	pub const SYS_KILL: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 15;
80	/// PM → kernel: fetch the next proc with pending kernel signals (slice 4.5).
81	/// Reply payload: target endpoint in `0..4` (i32; `NONE` when nothing is
82	/// pending) and the pending-signal bitmap in `4..8` (u32). The kernel hands
83	/// the bitmap off (clears `Proc::sig_pending`) but leaves the target's
84	/// signal-pending RTS state set until `SYS_ENDKSIG` acknowledges it.
85	pub const SYS_GETKSIG: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 16;
86	/// PM → kernel: signal processing for the target (payload `0..4`, i32) is
87	/// complete — clear its signal-pending RTS state (slice 4.5).
88	pub const SYS_ENDKSIG: i32 = KERNEL_CALL + 17;
89	
90	/// `SYS_SCHEDCTL` flag: revert the target to kernel scheduling
91	/// (`target.scheduler = NONE`). Absent → the caller claims the target as its
92	/// own scheduler. Matches MINIX 3 `SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL` (`include/minix/com.h`).
93	pub const SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL: i32 = 1 << 0;
94	
95	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
96	// `SYS_SAFECOPY` direction selector (payload `0..4`).
97	//
98	// One kernel-call number covers both directions, MINIX-style, because the
99	// validation and the copy engine are identical either way — only the source and
100	// destination swap. Numbered from 1 so a zeroed payload is an obvious
101	// "invalid", the `VMCTL_*` / `PRIVCTL_*` / `DIAGCTL_*` convention.
102	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
103	
104	/// Copy *out of* the granted range into the caller's buffer. Requires
105	/// `CPF_READ` on the grant.
106	pub const SAFECOPY_FROM: i32 = 1;
107	/// Copy *into* the granted range from the caller's buffer. Requires
108	/// `CPF_WRITE` on the grant.
109	pub const SAFECOPY_TO: i32 = 2;
110	
111	/// Length of the boot-embedded binary name carried in the `SYS_EXEC` payload
112	/// (`4..4+EXEC_NAME_LEN`), NUL-padded. Sized to fit the MXBI record name field
113	/// (`< 20` bytes); a short name like `"worker"` fits with room to spare.
114	pub const EXEC_NAME_LEN: usize = 16;
115	
116	/// Number of kernel calls defined. Reached 18 in Phase 4 (slice 4.3 made
117	/// `SYS_SCHEDULE` real and added `SYS_SCHEDCTL`; slice 4.5 added the signal
118	/// trio `SYS_KILL` / `SYS_GETKSIG` / `SYS_ENDKSIG`) and stays there through
119	/// Phase 5, which adds no new call numbers — it fills in bodies for calls that
120	/// were already numbered and `ENOSYS`-stubbed.
121	///
122	/// Named `NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4` until slice 5.1. The generated C header always
123	/// emitted it as `NR_KERN_CALLS`, and the two must not diverge past the slice
124	/// 5.6 ABI freeze.
125	pub const NR_KERN_CALLS: usize = 18;
126	
127	/// Size of the privilege-table kernel-call mask, in bits. Sized as a single
128	/// `u32` chunk (32 slots) to leave headroom past Phase 4's 15 calls while
129	/// keeping the bitmap a single word per privilege slot.
130	pub const NR_SYS_CALLS: usize = 32;
131	
132	const _: () = assert!(NR_SYS_CALLS >= NR_KERN_CALLS);
133	const _: () = assert!(NR_SYS_CALLS.is_multiple_of(32));
134	
135	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
136	// `SYS_GETINFO` request sub-types.
137	//
138	// `SYS_GETINFO` is a multi-purpose introspection call: the request sub-type
139	// in the first 4 bytes of the message payload selects what the kernel reports
140	// back. Numbering matches MINIX 3 `include/minix/sysinfo.h` so the same wire
141	// values can be reused once musl + servers land.
142	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
143	
144	/// `SYS_GETINFO` request: return the caller's endpoint, priv flags, init
145	/// flags, and process name. The kernel writes the reply into the payload of
146	/// the request message in-place; on return `m_type == OK`.
147	pub const GET_WHOAMI: i32 = 12;
148	
149	/// Length of the `name` field in the `GET_WHOAMI` reply payload. minix.rs uses
150	/// the kernel's own `PROC_NAME_LEN` here rather than MINIX 3's 44-byte field —
151	/// the name is only used for debug/log output and the kernel never stores more
152	/// than 16 bytes per slot.
153	pub const SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN: usize = 16;
154	
155	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
156	// `SYS_PRIVCTL` subcodes.
157	//
158	// `SYS_PRIVCTL` (real as of slice 4.5) sets up a target proc's privilege
159	// slot. The target endpoint lives in payload `0..4` and the subcode in `4..8`
160	// (both i32, the same target-first convention as `SYS_SCHEDULE`). Numbers
161	// start at 1 so a zeroed payload is an obvious "invalid" (the `VMCTL_*`
162	// convention). Modeled on MINIX 3 `SYS_PRIV_SET_USER`; the system-proc
163	// variants (`SET_SYS`, range grants) arrive with RS service starts.
164	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	
166	/// Point a frozen (`RTS_NO_PRIV`) target at the shared USER privilege slot
167	/// and release it. The USER slot carries `USR_T` traps, `ipc_to` = {PM}, and
168	/// an empty kernel-call mask — ordinary user processes make no kernel calls.
169	/// The 4.6 fork path leans on this to hand forked children a privilege.
170	pub const PRIVCTL_SET_USER: i32 = 1;
171	
172	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
173	// `SYS_DIAGCTL` subcodes + inline-text payload geometry.
174	//
175	// The subcode lives in payload `0..4` (the `GET_WHOAMI` / `VMCTL_*`
176	// convention), numbered from 1 so a zeroed payload is an obvious "invalid".
177	// Numbering follows MINIX 3's `DIAGCTL_CODE_*` order; only `DIAG` is
178	// implemented in Phase 5, the rest are reserved so their wire values cannot be
179	// reused by a later minix.rs-specific code.
180	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	
182	/// Print inline text to the kernel console. Length in payload `4..8`, text in
183	/// `DIAG_TEXT_OFF..DIAG_TEXT_OFF+len`.
184	pub const DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG: i32 = 1;
185	/// Reserved (MINIX 3 `DIAGCTL_CODE_STACKTRACE`) — `EINVAL` in Phase 5.
186	pub const DIAGCTL_CODE_STACKTRACE: i32 = 2;
187	/// Reserved (MINIX 3 `DIAGCTL_CODE_REGISTER`) — `EINVAL` in Phase 5.
188	pub const DIAGCTL_CODE_REGISTER: i32 = 3;
189	/// Reserved (MINIX 3 `DIAGCTL_CODE_UNREGISTER`) — `EINVAL` in Phase 5.
190	pub const DIAGCTL_CODE_UNREGISTER: i32 = 4;
191	
192	/// Offset of the inline text within the `SYS_DIAGCTL` payload. Follows the
193	/// subcode (`0..4`) and length (`4..8`) words, so the text starts 8-aligned.
194	pub const DIAG_TEXT_OFF: usize = 8;
195	
196	/// Maximum inline text bytes carried by one `SYS_DIAGCTL(DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG)`
197	/// call — the rest of the 96-byte payload. `server-rt::diag_print` splits
198	/// longer strings across successive calls, one console line each.
199	pub const DIAG_TEXT_MAX: usize = 96 - DIAG_TEXT_OFF;
200	
201	const _: () = assert!(DIAG_TEXT_OFF + DIAG_TEXT_MAX == 96);
202	
203	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
204	// `SYS_VMCTL` subcalls.
205	//
206	// `SYS_VMCTL` mediates all user-space page-table changes: the kernel owns the
207	// physical frame allocator and every unsafe PTE write, and VM (slice 3.4)
208	// drives policy by issuing these subcalls. The subcall selector lives in the
209	// first 4 bytes of the message payload (same convention as `GET_WHOAMI`); the
210	// target process is named by an endpoint in the next 4 bytes (`SELF` allowed).
211	// Numbers start at 1 so a zeroed payload (subcall 0) is an obvious "invalid".
212	// These are minix.rs-specific — MINIX 3's VMCTL subcall set differs because its
213	// frame allocator lives in VM, not the kernel.
214	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
215	
216	/// Allocate a fresh zeroed frame and map it at `vaddr` in the target's
217	/// address space with the requested protection. The allocated PA is returned
218	/// in the reply payload. (The kernel allocates because the frame allocator is
219	/// kernel-side; VM supplies only `vaddr` + protection.)
220	pub const VMCTL_PT_MAP: i32 = 1;
221	/// Unmap `vaddr` in the target's address space and free the backing frame.
222	pub const VMCTL_PT_UNMAP: i32 = 2;
223	/// Clear the target's pending page fault and make it runnable again.
224	pub const VMCTL_CLEAR_PAGEFAULT: i32 = 3;
225	/// Read the target's recorded page-fault state (addr/flags/ip) into the reply.
226	/// Valid only while the target is blocked on a page fault.
227	pub const VMCTL_GET_PAGEFAULT: i32 = 4;
228	/// Inhibit scheduling of the target while VM mutates its address space.
229	pub const VMCTL_VMINHIBIT_SET: i32 = 5;
230	/// Release a prior `VMCTL_VMINHIBIT_SET`.
231	pub const VMCTL_VMINHIBIT_CLEAR: i32 = 6;
232	
233	/// Number of `SYS_VMCTL` subcalls. Locks the dispatch-match coverage in
234	/// `system::do_vmctl` via a const-assert.
235	pub const NR_VMCTL_SUBCALLS: usize = 6;
236	
237	// `VMCTL_PT_MAP` protection bits (message payload, `vaddr`-adjacent word).
238	/// EL0 may write the mapped page.
239	pub const VMCTL_PROT_WRITE: i32 = 1 << 0;
240	/// EL0 may execute from the mapped page.
241	pub const VMCTL_PROT_EXEC: i32 = 1 << 1;
242	
243	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
244	// PM (process manager) server request numbers — `m_type` values for messages
245	// addressed to the PM server (slice 4.5).
246	//
247	// Like the VM/DS/SEF/SCHED ranges these are *server IPC requests*, not kernel
248	// calls. SCHED's `0xF00` block is the last one below the IPC `NOTIFY_MESSAGE`
249	// marker (`0x1000`), so PM takes the free gap between the kernel-call range
250	// (`0x600..0x618`) and VM (`0xC00`). Numbering is minix.rs-specific — MINIX 3
251	// carries PM call numbers in `callnr.h`; those ABI numbers arrive with the
252	// musl wrappers in Phase 5.
253	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
254	
255	/// Base for PM server request `m_type` values.
256	pub const PM_RQ_BASE: i32 = 0x700;
257	
258	/// Client → PM: return the caller's process id. No request payload — the
259	/// kernel-stamped `m_source` names the caller. Reply: `m_type` *is* the pid
260	/// (MINIX convention: the result is the pid, >= 0; errors are negative, e.g.
261	/// `ESRCH` for a caller unknown to PM's mproc table), with the parent's pid
262	/// in payload `0..4` (i32) so `getppid` needs no second call.
263	pub const PM_GETPID: i32 = PM_RQ_BASE;
264	
265	/// User → PM: `fork()`. No request payload — the kernel-stamped `m_source` names
266	/// the parent. PM allocates a child slot, drives `SYS_FORK` + `VM_FORK` +
267	/// `SCHEDULING_START` + `SYS_PRIVCTL(PRIVCTL_SET_USER)`, then replies to **both**
268	/// halves of the shared blocked SENDREC: the child receives `m_type = 0`, the
269	/// parent receives `m_type = child_pid` (MINIX fork-returns-twice). On failure
270	/// the parent's reply carries a negative errno (`EAGAIN` if PM's process table
271	/// is full). (slice 4.6b)
272	pub const PM_FORK: i32 = PM_RQ_BASE + 1;
273	
274	/// User → PM: `exit(status)`. Exit status in payload `0..4` (i32). PM tears the
275	/// caller down (`SCHEDULING_STOP` + `SYS_EXIT`) and either wakes a `wait()`ing
276	/// parent or leaves a zombie for the parent's next `wait()`. The caller is dead
277	/// after `SYS_EXIT`, so PM sends **no** reply. (slice 4.6b)
278	pub const PM_EXIT: i32 = PM_RQ_BASE + 2;
279	
280	/// User → PM: `wait()` for any child. No request payload — `m_source` names the
281	/// parent. If a zombie child exists PM reaps it and replies immediately;
282	/// otherwise, with a live child, PM suspends the caller (no reply) until the
283	/// child exits. Reply: `m_type` *is* the reaped child's pid (>= 0), with the
284	/// encoded exit status in payload `0..4` (i32, `(status & 0xff) << 8`), or
285	/// `ECHILD` in `m_type` if the caller has no children. (slice 4.6b)
286	pub const PM_WAIT: i32 = PM_RQ_BASE + 3;
287	
288	/// User → PM: `execve()`. No request payload in the slice-4.7 demo — PM selects
289	/// the boot-embedded target (`"worker"`) and issues `SYS_EXEC` naming the
290	/// caller. PM sends **no** reply on success (the kernel resumes the caller at
291	/// the new image's entry point); on failure the reply `m_type` carries a
292	/// negative errno and the caller continues in its old image. A user-supplied
293	/// path arrives with the filesystem/musl wrappers in Phase 5. (slice 4.7)
294	pub const PM_EXEC: i32 = PM_RQ_BASE + 4;
295	
296	/// VFS → PM: the slice-5.2 grant demo. Carries a grant id in-band, which is how
297	/// grant ids really travel — slice 5.3's `CDEV_WRITE {minor, granter, grant_id,
298	/// len}` is the same shape. (DS cannot carry one: `DS_PUBLISH` deliberately
299	/// registers the kernel-stamped `m_source` and ignores the payload, which is
300	/// precisely its anti-spoof property.)
301	///
302	/// Payload: grant id in `0..4` (i32), granted length in `4..8` (i32), a second
303	/// grant id in `8..12` (i32) that deliberately claims `CPF_WRITE` over the same
304	/// read-only buffer for PM's denial probe, and the granter's raw buffer address
305	/// in `16..24` (u64) for the ungranted `SYS_COPY` comparison.
306	///
307	/// The **granter is not in the payload**: PM takes it from the kernel-stamped
308	/// `m_source`, the same anti-spoof property `DS_PUBLISH` relies on. It matters
309	/// here because PM holds `SYS_COPY` / `SYS_SAFECOPY` and its clients do not — a
310	/// caller-supplied granter endpoint would let any PM client aim a privileged
311	/// copy at a third party's address space through PM (a confused deputy). PM
312	/// additionally serves this request only when `m_source` is VFS.
313	///
314	/// Sent with `ipc_send`, so the sender blocks until PM's loop picks it up and
315	/// the demo is self-synchronizing; PM sends no reply. **Demo-only** — retire it
316	/// when a real grant consumer (CDEV, slice 5.3) lands.
317	pub const PM_GRANT_TEST: i32 = PM_RQ_BASE + 5;
318	
319	/// Number of PM server requests defined so far. Locks the PM server's
320	/// dispatch coverage the way `NR_DS_REQUESTS` locks the DS server.
321	pub const NR_PM_MSGS: usize = 6;
322	
323	// The PM range sits strictly above the kernel-call range and strictly below
324	// VM's (and therefore every other) server request range and the NOTIFY marker.
325	const _: () = assert!(PM_RQ_BASE > KERNEL_CALL + (NR_KERN_CALLS as i32 - 1));
326	const _: () = assert!(PM_RQ_BASE + (NR_PM_MSGS as i32 - 1) < VM_RQ_BASE);
327	const _: () = assert!(PM_RQ_BASE + (NR_PM_MSGS as i32 - 1) < crate::ipc_const::NOTIFY_MESSAGE);
328	
329	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
330	// VM server request numbers — `m_type` values for messages addressed to VM.
331	//
332	// These are *server IPC requests*, not kernel calls, so they live in their own
333	// range distinct from `KERNEL_CALL` (`0x600`). The kernel originates
334	// `VM_PAGEFAULT` on a faulting process's behalf (slice 3.4); later slices add
335	// `VM_BRK` / `VM_MMAP` / `VM_MUNMAP`. Numbering is minix.rs-specific (MINIX 3's VM request set
336	// differs because its frame allocator lives in VM, not the kernel).
337	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
338	
339	/// Base for VM server request `m_type` values.
340	pub const VM_RQ_BASE: i32 = 0xC00;
341	
342	/// Kernel → VM: a process page-faulted. `m_source` identifies the faulting
343	/// process; the payload carries the fault address (`0..8`, u64) and fault
344	/// flags (`8..12`, u32). VM resolves it via `SYS_VMCTL(VMCTL_PT_MAP)` +
345	/// `SYS_VMCTL(VMCTL_CLEAR_PAGEFAULT)`.
346	pub const VM_PAGEFAULT: i32 = VM_RQ_BASE;
347	
348	/// EL0 → VM: set the caller's program break to `new_break` (payload `0..8`,
349	/// u64). VM grows or creates the caller's heap region to `[HEAP_BASE,
350	/// new_break)`; pages fault in lazily on first touch (no eager mapping). The
351	/// reply carries `m_type = OK` and the resulting break in payload `0..8`, or a
352	/// negative error in `m_type`. (slice 3.5)
353	pub const VM_BRK: i32 = VM_RQ_BASE + 1;
354	
355	/// EL0 → VM: anonymous mmap. The caller requests `len` bytes (payload `0..8`,
356	/// u64); VM page-aligns the length, picks a free VA from the caller's mmap bump
357	/// arena, records an `Mmap` region, and replies with the chosen base address in
358	/// payload `0..8` and `m_type = OK`. Like `mmap(NULL, len, …)`: VM chooses the
359	/// address. Pages fault in lazily on first touch (no eager mapping). On failure
360	/// the negative error is in `m_type` (`EINVAL` for a zero or overflowing
361	/// length, `ENOMEM` when no region slot is free). (slice 3.6)
362	pub const VM_MMAP: i32 = VM_RQ_BASE + 2;
363	
364	/// EL0 → VM: unmap a prior mmap. The caller passes the base address (payload
365	/// `0..8`, u64) and length (payload `8..16`, u64). VM page-aligns the range,
366	/// drops the matching `Mmap` region, and unmaps each backing page via
367	/// `SYS_VMCTL(VMCTL_PT_UNMAP)` (a never-faulted page returns a harmless
368	/// `EINVAL` from the kernel, which VM ignores). The reply carries
369	/// `m_type = OK`, or `EINVAL` in `m_type` if no `Mmap` region matches the base
370	/// address. (slice 3.6)
371	pub const VM_MUNMAP: i32 = VM_RQ_BASE + 3;
372	
373	/// PM → VM: clone a parent's memory region set into a freshly forked child.
374	/// The kernel already copied the child's page tables (`SYS_FORK`); this copies
375	/// VM's own bookkeeping so the child's later brk/mmap/fault lookups see the
376	/// inherited heap/mmap regions. Payload: parent endpoint (`0..4`, i32), child
377	/// endpoint (`4..8`, i32). Reply `m_type = OK`, or `EINVAL` in `m_type` if
378	/// either endpoint maps to an out-of-range proc number. (slice 4.6b)
379	pub const VM_FORK: i32 = VM_RQ_BASE + 4;
380	
381	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
382	// DS (Data Store) server request numbers — `m_type` values for messages
383	// addressed to the DS server.
384	//
385	// DS is a name→endpoint registry: every server publishes its own endpoint at
386	// init (slice 4.2) so others can look each other up without hard-coding boot
387	// proc numbers. These are *server IPC requests* like the VM range, so they live
388	// in their own range, distinct from `KERNEL_CALL` (`0x600`), the VM request
389	// range (`VM_RQ_BASE = 0xC00`), and the SEF control range (`SEF_RQ_BASE =
390	// 0xD00`), and stay below the IPC `NOTIFY_MESSAGE` marker (`0x1000`) so neither
391	// a server's `m_type` dispatcher nor the SEF classifier can ever misroute.
392	//
393	// The key (a NUL-padded server name) travels inline in the request payload
394	// (`0..SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN`); no grants / cross-AS copy are needed because the
395	// kernel copies the whole 96-byte payload on delivery. An endpoint value rides
396	// in payload `16..20` (i32, native-endian) only on `DS_RETRIEVE` replies;
397	// `DS_PUBLISH` registers the caller's kernel-stamped `m_source` (a process can
398	// only publish itself), so no endpoint is sent in a publish request. Numbering
399	// is minix.rs-specific.
400	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
401	
402	/// Base for DS server request `m_type` values.
403	pub const DS_RQ_BASE: i32 = 0xE00;
404	
405	/// Server → DS: publish the *caller's own* endpoint under the key in payload
406	/// `0..SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN`. DS records the caller's kernel-stamped `m_source`,
407	/// not a value from the payload, so a process can only publish itself and can
408	/// never spoof another server's endpoint. Re-publishing the same key updates the
409	/// stored endpoint. Reply `m_type = OK`, or `EINVAL` (empty key) / `ENOMEM`
410	/// (registry full).
411	pub const DS_PUBLISH: i32 = DS_RQ_BASE;
412	
413	/// Client → DS: look up the endpoint for the key in payload `0..NAME_LEN`.
414	/// Reply `m_type = OK` with the endpoint in payload `16..20` (i32), or
415	/// `ESRCH` if the key is not registered.
416	pub const DS_RETRIEVE: i32 = DS_RQ_BASE + 1;
417	
418	/// Client → DS: test whether the key in payload `0..NAME_LEN` is registered.
419	/// Reply `m_type = OK` with a status in payload `16..20` (i32: 1 = present,
420	/// 0 = absent) — absence is a status, not an error, so a `CHECK` never aborts
421	/// the caller's SENDREC.
422	pub const DS_CHECK: i32 = DS_RQ_BASE + 2;
423	
424	/// Number of DS server requests defined so far. Locks the dispatch-match
425	/// coverage in the DS server the way `NR_VMCTL_SUBCALLS` locks `do_vmctl`.
426	pub const NR_DS_REQUESTS: usize = 3;
427	
428	// The DS range sits strictly above the SEF range (0xD00..0xD01) so a server's
429	// `m_type` dispatcher and the SEF classifier can never collide, and stays
430	// below the NOTIFY marker.
431	const _: () = assert!(DS_RQ_BASE > SEF_RQ_BASE + (NR_SEF_MSGS as i32 - 1));
432	const _: () = assert!(DS_RQ_BASE + (NR_DS_REQUESTS as i32 - 1) < crate::ipc_const::NOTIFY_MESSAGE);
433	
434	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
435	// SEF (System Event Framework) control message numbers — `m_type` values the
436	// server runtime (`server-rt`) intercepts before handing traffic to a server.
437	//
438	// These live in their own range distinct from `KERNEL_CALL` (`0x600`) and the
439	// VM request range (`VM_RQ_BASE = 0xC00`), and stay below the IPC
440	// `NOTIFY_MESSAGE` marker (`0x1000`), so neither a server's `m_type`
441	// dispatcher nor the SEF classifier can ever misroute. Numbering is
442	// minix.rs-specific (MINIX 3 carries these inside `lib/libsys/sef.c` request
443	// types rather than `com.h`).
444	//
445	// The RS heartbeat ("ping") deliberately gets NO number here: it is delivered
446	// as a NOTIFY, so it arrives with `m_type == NOTIFY_MESSAGE` and is keyed on
447	// `m_source == RS` instead (see `server-rt`'s `classify`). Do not add a
448	// `SEF_PING` — there is no payload room in a NOTIFY to carry one anyway.
449	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
450	
451	/// Base for SEF control message `m_type` values.
452	pub const SEF_RQ_BASE: i32 = 0xD00;
453	
454	/// RS → server: run the registered fresh-init callback. (Re-init / live-update
455	/// variants are deferred past Phase 4.)
456	pub const SEF_INIT: i32 = SEF_RQ_BASE;
457	
458	/// PM/RS → server: deliver a signal. The signal number is in payload `0..4`
459	/// (i32, native-endian); `server-rt` dispatches it to the registered signal
460	/// handler.
461	pub const SEF_SIGNAL: i32 = SEF_RQ_BASE + 1;
462	
463	/// Number of SEF control messages defined so far. Locks the classifier's
464	/// coverage in `server-rt` the way `NR_VMCTL_SUBCALLS` locks `do_vmctl`.
465	pub const NR_SEF_MSGS: usize = 2;
466	
467	// The SEF range sits strictly above the VM request range (0xC00..0xC04) so a
468	// server's `m_type` dispatcher and the SEF classifier can never collide.
469	const _: () = assert!(SEF_RQ_BASE > VM_RQ_BASE + 4);
470	const _: () = assert!(SEF_RQ_BASE < crate::ipc_const::NOTIFY_MESSAGE);
471	
472	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
473	// SCHED (scheduler) server request numbers — `m_type` values for messages
474	// addressed to the user-space SCHED server (slice 4.3).
475	//
476	// `SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM` is kernel-originated: when a SCHED-scheduled proc
477	// exhausts its quantum, the kernel sends it (with `m_source` = the preempted
478	// proc, so SCHED knows which proc to reschedule), exactly as it originates
479	// `VM_PAGEFAULT` for a faulter. The other three are PM/RS → SCHED requests
480	// (claim/release/renice a managed proc). Like the VM/DS ranges these are
481	// *server IPC requests*, not kernel calls, so they live in their own range
482	// distinct from `KERNEL_CALL` (`0x600`), VM (`0xC00`), SEF (`0xD00`), and DS
483	// (`0xE00`), and stay below the IPC `NOTIFY_MESSAGE` marker (`0x1000`) so the
484	// SEF classifier (which returns `Application` for them) can never misroute.
485	// Numbering is minix.rs-specific (MINIX 3 carries `SCHEDULING_*` in `com.h`).
486	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
487	
488	/// Base for SCHED server request `m_type` values.
489	pub const SCHED_RQ_BASE: i32 = 0xF00;
490	
491	/// Kernel → SCHED: the proc identified by `m_source` used up its full quantum.
492	/// SCHED applies its policy and re-admits the proc via `SYS_SCHEDULE`. Carries
493	/// no payload — `m_source` is the whole request.
494	pub const SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM: i32 = SCHED_RQ_BASE;
495	
496	/// PM/RS → SCHED: start scheduling a proc. The target endpoint is in payload
497	/// `0..4` (i32), the initial priority in `4..8` (i32), and the quantum (ms) in
498	/// `8..12` (i32). SCHED claims the target via `SYS_SCHEDCTL` and assigns the
499	/// initial priority/quantum via `SYS_SCHEDULE`. (Driven by PM/RS from slice 4.5+.)
500	pub const SCHEDULING_START: i32 = SCHED_RQ_BASE + 1;
501	
502	/// PM/RS → SCHED: stop scheduling the target (payload `0..4`, i32). SCHED hands
503	/// it back to the kernel scheduler via `SYS_SCHEDCTL(SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL)`.
504	pub const SCHEDULING_STOP: i32 = SCHED_RQ_BASE + 2;
505	
506	/// PM/RS → SCHED: change the target's nice value. Target endpoint in payload
507	/// `0..4` (i32), new priority in `4..8` (i32). SCHED records it and applies it
508	/// via `SYS_SCHEDULE`.
509	pub const SCHEDULING_SET_NICE: i32 = SCHED_RQ_BASE + 3;
510	
511	/// Number of SCHED server requests defined so far. Locks the dispatch-match
512	/// coverage in the SCHED server the way `NR_DS_REQUESTS` locks the DS server.
513	pub const NR_SCHED_MSGS: usize = 4;
514	
515	// The SCHED range sits strictly above the DS range (0xE00..0xE02) and below the
516	// NOTIFY marker, so neither a server's `m_type` dispatcher nor the SEF
517	// classifier can ever collide with it.
518	const _: () = assert!(SCHED_RQ_BASE > DS_RQ_BASE + (NR_DS_REQUESTS as i32 - 1));
519	const _: () =
520	    assert!(SCHED_RQ_BASE + (NR_SCHED_MSGS as i32 - 1) < crate::ipc_const::NOTIFY_MESSAGE);

3	//! Per-process memory regions tracked by the VM server (slice 3.5).
4	//!
5	//! VM is the user-space authority on what virtual addresses a process may
6	//! touch. Before slice 3.5 it resolved *every* page fault by blindly mapping a
7	//! fresh page; now it consults a per-process region table so that only faults
8	//! inside a known region (today: the heap) are satisfied. Out-of-region faults
9	//! are a SIGSEGV (handled by the caller in `main.rs`).
10	//!
11	//! The table is a static `[ClientRegions; MAX_CLIENTS]` indexed by process
12	//! number. This mirrors the kernel's `PROC_TABLE` convention: an
13	//! `UnsafeCell<[T; N]>` inside a `#[repr(transparent)]` newtype with
14	//! `unsafe impl Sync`. The single-mutator invariant is even simpler here than
15	//! in the kernel — VM is a single EL0 thread with no interrupt handlers of its
16	//! own (IRQs trap into the kernel, never into VM), so the table is only ever
17	//! touched from VM's straight-line receive loop.
18	//!
19	//! `MAX_CLIENTS` is sized from the shared [`NR_SERVED_PROCS`] ceiling so the
20	//! table covers the whole proc-number range the user-space servers track: the
21	//! boot procs and stubs `0..15` plus PM's fork pool `[15, NR_SERVED_PROCS)`
22	//! (`VM_FORK` records a child's inherited regions keyed by its proc number). A
23	//! full `NR_PROCS`-slot table would burn hundreds of KiB of BSS the ELF loader
24	//! must map at boot; the shared ceiling keeps it right-sized and in lockstep
25	//! with PM's mproc table.
26	
27	use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
28	
29	use minixrs_kernel_shared::com::NR_SERVED_PROCS;
30	use minixrs_kernel_shared::error::{EINVAL, ENOMEM};
31	
32	/// Fixed heap origin. Until PM supplies a real per-process memory layout
33	/// (Phase 4), VM and stub D agree on this VA by convention: `brk` grows the
34	/// heap as `[HEAP_BASE, new_break)` and stub D writes inside that range.
35	pub const HEAP_BASE: u64 = 0x0100_0000;
36	
37	/// Origin of the per-process anonymous-mmap arena. VM bump-allocates mmap
38	/// addresses upward from here, so a mapping never collides with stub D's code
39	/// (`0x0043_0000`), stack (`0x0083_0000`), or heap
40	/// (`[0x0100_0000, 0x0100_8000)` today). `0x0200_0000` sits a clean 16 MiB above
41	/// `HEAP_BASE`, leaving the heap room to grow before it could reach the arena.
42	/// The arena itself is bump-only — munmap never returns addresses to it (reuse
43	/// waits for Phase 4's real per-process VM layout), so an unbounded mmap loop
44	/// would eventually walk off the end; acceptable while only the boot stubs run.
45	pub const MMAP_BASE: u64 = 0x0200_0000;
46	
47	/// aarch64 4 KiB page.
48	const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
49	
50	/// Proc-number range the table can key. Boot procs and stubs occupy `0..15`; PM
51	/// allocates forked children from the pool above that (kernel proc-nr = PM mproc
52	/// slot, `[15, NR_SERVED_PROCS)` — see `servers/pm/src/mproc.rs`), so the table
53	/// must cover the whole fork pool for `VM_FORK` to record a child's inherited
54	/// regions. Derived from the shared ceiling; the guard below rejects any local
55	/// under-sizing that would leave a PM-allocatable child unaddressable here.
56	const MAX_CLIENTS: usize = NR_SERVED_PROCS;
57	
58	const _: () = assert!(MAX_CLIENTS >= NR_SERVED_PROCS);
59	
60	/// Regions tracked per process: one heap plus several `mmap` regions in the
61	/// spare slots. Sixteen leaves room for a loader's segments, a heap, a stack,
62	/// and a handful of anonymous mmaps once Phase 5 runs real programs.
63	const MAX_REGIONS: usize = 16;
64	
65	/// What a region is for. `Unused` marks a free slot.
66	#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
67	pub enum Kind {
68	    Unused,
69	    Heap,
70	    Mmap,
71	}
72	
73	/// A half-open virtual-address range `[start, end)` and what it backs.
74	#[derive(Copy, Clone)]
75	struct Region {
76	    start: u64,
77	    end: u64,
78	    kind: Kind,
79	}
80	
81	impl Region {
82	    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
83	        start: 0,
84	        end: 0,
85	        kind: Kind::Unused,
86	    };
87	
88	    fn contains(&self, addr: u64) -> bool {
89	        self.kind != Kind::Unused && addr >= self.start && addr < self.end
90	    }
91	}
92	
93	/// One process's region set.
94	#[derive(Copy, Clone)]
95	struct ClientRegions {

99	    /// Phase 4's real VM layout).

101	}
102	
103	impl ClientRegions {
104	    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
105	        regions: [Region::EMPTY; MAX_REGIONS],
106	        mmap_next: MMAP_BASE,
107	    };

+// narrower (no `CDEV_REPLY` message class; a driver replies to the SENDREC).

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! 8-bit ARMv8 ASID allocator with recycling.
4	//!
5	//! TTBR0_EL1 carries an ASID in bits [55:48] when TCR_EL1.AS = 0 (Limine's
6	//! default; `mmu::assert_tcr_el1_ttbr0_ready` enforces). The TLB tags
7	//! entries by ASID, so context switches that flip TTBR0 don't need a full
8	//! TLB flush — only a `tlbi aside1, Xt` of stale entries for the activated
9	//! ASID.
10	//!
11	//! Boot allocates ~11 ASIDs (six archive servers + five EL0 stubs), but
12	//! slice 4.6's fork/exit churn would exhaust the 8-bit space (1..=255,
13	//! ASID 0 reserved for "uninitialized") within minutes without recycling.
14	//! `SYS_EXIT` therefore returns each dead process's ASID via [`free_asid`]
15	//! (after flushing its TLB entries), and [`alloc_asid`] serves from that
16	//! free list before minting fresh IDs. Exhaustion — 255 simultaneously
17	//! *live* address spaces — still panics; that is a real capacity invariant,
18	//! not a churn artifact.
19	//!
20	//! Concurrency: single-threaded boot, like the rest of the kernel. Wrapped
21	//! in `UnsafeCell` + `unsafe impl Sync` per the convention documented on
22	//! `crate::proc::table`.
23	
24	use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
25	
26	/// First real ASID handed out. 0 is reserved as the "uninitialized"
27	/// sentinel `Proc::asid` carries until `userland_bootstrap` assigns a real
28	/// value.
29	const FIRST_ASID: u8 = 1;
30	
31	/// One past the highest ASID (the 8-bit hardware limit).
32	const ASID_LIMIT: u16 = 256;
33	
34	struct AsidPool {
35	    /// Next never-yet-minted ASID; grows monotonically to [`ASID_LIMIT`].
36	    next: u16,
37	    /// LIFO stack of freed ASIDs available for reuse.
38	    free: [u8; (ASID_LIMIT - 1) as usize],
39	    free_len: usize,
40	}
41	
42	#[repr(transparent)]
43	struct AsidPoolCell(UnsafeCell<AsidPool>);
44	// SAFETY: single-threaded EL1 (interrupts masked in every kernel entry
45	// path); `alloc_asid`/`free_asid` are the only accessors.
46	unsafe impl Sync for AsidPoolCell {}
47	
48	static POOL: AsidPoolCell = AsidPoolCell(UnsafeCell::new(AsidPool {
49	    next: FIRST_ASID as u16,
50	    free: [0; (ASID_LIMIT - 1) as usize],
51	    free_len: 0,
52	}));
53	
54	/// Hand out an ASID: recycled from the free list if one is available, else
55	/// freshly minted. Panics when 255 address spaces are simultaneously live.
56	///
57	/// SAFETY: caller must hold the single-threaded EL1 invariant; this and
58	/// [`free_asid`] are the sole accessors of the pool.
59	pub unsafe fn alloc_asid() -> u8 {
60	    // SAFETY: caller's invariant — no concurrent pool access.
61	    let pool = unsafe { &mut *POOL.0.get() };
62	    if pool.free_len > 0 {
63	        pool.free_len -= 1;
64	        return pool.free[pool.free_len];
65	    }
66	    assert!(
67	        pool.next < ASID_LIMIT,
68	        "ASID space exhausted: 255 live address spaces"
69	    );
70	    let id = pool.next as u8;
71	    pool.next += 1;
72	    id
73	}
74	
75	/// Return a dead process's ASID to the pool for reuse.
76	///
77	/// Contract: the caller must already have invalidated the ASID's TLB entries
78	/// (`mmu::flush_tlb_asid`) — the next `alloc_asid` may hand this ID to a
79	/// brand-new address space, and a stale translation would alias it. A
80	/// double-free would eventually let two live procs share one ASID (same
81	/// aliasing corruption), so it is a hard assert, not a debug one — the O(255)
82	/// scan is noise next to the page-table teardown that precedes every call.
83	///
84	/// SAFETY: caller must hold the single-threaded EL1 invariant; this and
85	/// [`alloc_asid`] are the sole accessors of the pool.
86	pub unsafe fn free_asid(asid: u8) {
87	    assert!(asid != 0, "freeing the reserved ASID 0");
88	    // SAFETY: caller's invariant — no concurrent pool access.
89	    let pool = unsafe { &mut *POOL.0.get() };
90	    assert!(
91	        (asid as u16) < pool.next,
92	        "freeing ASID {asid} that was never allocated"
93	    );
94	    for i in 0..pool.free_len {
95	        assert!(pool.free[i] != asid, "double free of ASID {asid}");
96	    }
97	    pool.free[pool.free_len] = asid;
98	    pool.free_len += 1;
99	}

3	//! Per-process memory regions tracked by the VM server (slice 3.5).
4	//!
5	//! VM is the user-space authority on what virtual addresses a process may
6	//! touch. Before slice 3.5 it resolved *every* page fault by blindly mapping a
7	//! fresh page; now it consults a per-process region table so that only faults
8	//! inside a known region (today: the heap) are satisfied. Out-of-region faults
9	//! are a SIGSEGV (handled by the caller in `main.rs`).
10	//!
11	//! The table is a static `[ClientRegions; MAX_CLIENTS]` indexed by process
12	//! number. This mirrors the kernel's `PROC_TABLE` convention: an
13	//! `UnsafeCell<[T; N]>` inside a `#[repr(transparent)]` newtype with
14	//! `unsafe impl Sync`. The single-mutator invariant is even simpler here than
15	//! in the kernel — VM is a single EL0 thread with no interrupt handlers of its
16	//! own (IRQs trap into the kernel, never into VM), so the table is only ever
17	//! touched from VM's straight-line receive loop.
18	//!
19	//! `MAX_CLIENTS` is sized from the shared [`NR_SERVED_PROCS`] ceiling so the
20	//! table covers the whole proc-number range the user-space servers track: the
21	//! boot procs and stubs `0..15` plus PM's fork pool `[15, NR_SERVED_PROCS)`
22	//! (`VM_FORK` records a child's inherited regions keyed by its proc number). A
23	//! full `NR_PROCS`-slot table would burn hundreds of KiB of BSS the ELF loader
24	//! must map at boot; the shared ceiling keeps it right-sized and in lockstep
25	//! with PM's mproc table.
26	
27	use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
28	
29	use minixrs_kernel_shared::com::NR_SERVED_PROCS;
30	use minixrs_kernel_shared::error::{EINVAL, ENOMEM};
31	use minixrs_kernel_shared::uspace::USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE;
32	
33	/// Fixed heap origin. Until PM supplies a real per-process memory layout
34	/// (Phase 4), VM and stub D agree on this VA by convention: `brk` grows the
35	/// heap as `[HEAP_BASE, new_break)` and stub D writes inside that range.
36	pub const HEAP_BASE: u64 = 0x0100_0000;
37	
38	/// Origin of the per-process anonymous-mmap arena. VM bump-allocates mmap
39	/// addresses upward from here, so a mapping never collides with stub D's code
40	/// (`0x0043_0000`), stack (`0x0083_0000`), or heap
41	/// (`[0x0100_0000, 0x0100_8000)` today). `0x0200_0000` sits a clean 16 MiB above
42	/// `HEAP_BASE`, leaving the heap room to grow before it could reach the arena.
43	///
44	/// The arena is bump-only — munmap never returns addresses to it (reuse waits for
45	/// a real per-process VM layout). Since slice 5.3 it is **capped** at
46	/// [`MMAP_LIMIT`] rather than growing without bound: the kernel now pre-maps a
47	/// device window at [`USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE`], and an unbounded mmap loop would
48	/// eventually hand a client an address inside it. Past the cap, `mmap` returns
49	/// `ENOMEM`.
50	pub const MMAP_BASE: u64 = 0x0200_0000;
51	
52	/// Exclusive upper bound of the anonymous-mmap arena: the base of the kernel's
53	/// user-space device window (slice 5.3). A `const _` alone would not be enough
54	/// here — it would prove only that the arena *starts* below the window, and the
55	/// bump cursor grows.
56	pub const MMAP_LIMIT: u64 = USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE;
57	
58	// The arena must start below the device window, or every mmap would land inside
59	// it and `MMAP_LIMIT` would reject the first request.
60	const _: () = assert!(MMAP_BASE < USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE);
61	
62	/// aarch64 4 KiB page.
63	const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
64	
65	/// Proc-number range the table can key. Boot procs and stubs occupy `0..15`; PM
66	/// allocates forked children from the pool above that (kernel proc-nr = PM mproc

70	/// under-sizing that would leave a PM-allocatable child unaddressable here.
71	const MAX_CLIENTS: usize = NR_SERVED_PROCS;
72	
73	const _: () = assert!(MAX_CLIENTS >= NR_SERVED_PROCS);

76	/// spare slots. Sixteen leaves room for a loader's segments, a heap, a stack,
77	/// and a handful of anonymous mmaps once Phase 5 runs real programs.
78	const MAX_REGIONS: usize = 16;

80	/// What a region is for. `Unused` marks a free slot.
81	#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
82	pub enum Kind {
83	    Unused,
84	    Heap,
85	    Mmap,
86	}

88	/// A half-open virtual-address range `[start, end)` and what it backs.
89	#[derive(Copy, Clone)]
90	struct Region {
91	    start: u64,
92	    end: u64,
93	    kind: Kind,
94	}

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! The user-space virtual-address map the kernel and user space agree on.
4	//!
5	//! Everything else in this crate describes a *message* ABI — bytes on the wire
6	//! between two processes. This module describes an *address* ABI: the kernel
7	//! installs a mapping at one of these VAs and a user-space process dereferences
8	//! it, with no message in between. Slice 5.3's TTY driver is the first consumer:
9	//! the kernel pre-maps the PL011 MMIO page at [`TTY_UART_VA`] with Device
10	//! attributes while building TTY's address space, and TTY's `pl011.rs` does
11	//! volatile loads and stores there.
12	//!
13	//! That is why this is not in [`crate::message`]: nothing here is a payload
14	//! offset or a pointer predicate, and getting a value wrong is a data abort in
15	//! user space, not a rejected message.
16	//!
17	//! ## The device window
18	//!
19	//! [`USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE`] carves one whole L1 slot (1 GiB of VA space,
20	//! costing exactly one L1 + L2 + L3 frame for the pages actually mapped) out of
21	//! the user VA range, well clear of every VA any process occupies today:
22	//!
23	//! | VA | What |
24	//! |---|---|
25	//! | `0x0010_0000` | server / init / worker ELF images (`user.ld` base) |
26	//! | `0x0020_0000` | server stack page (`SERVER_STACK_VA`) |
27	//! | `0x0040_0000` / `0x0080_0000` | demo stub code / stack pages |
28	//! | `0x0100_0000` | VM's heap origin (`region::HEAP_BASE`) |
29	//! | `0x0200_0000` | VM's anonymous-mmap arena (`region::MMAP_BASE`) |
30	//! | `0x4000_0000` | **this window** |
31	//!
32	//! VM's mmap arena is the only one of those that grows, and it is bump-only, so
33	//! `servers/vm/src/region.rs` caps it at [`USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE`] rather than
34	//! relying on the 992 MiB of slack.
35	//!
36	//! Phase 6's virtio-mmio drivers get further pages of the same window; the
37	//! 16 MiB size is sized for that rather than for TTY's single page.
38	//!
39	//! These constants are deliberately **not** emitted into the generated C headers:
40	//! no Phase 5 C touches them (musl's `write()` goes to VFS, not to a driver's
41	//! MMIO window), and a header constant is an ABI promise that would be awkward to
42	//! retract once Phase 6 reshapes the window.
43	
44	use crate::message::{USER_PAGE_SIZE, USER_VA_TOP};
45	
46	/// Base of the user-space device (MMIO) window. One whole L1 slot at 1 GiB.
47	pub const USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE: u64 = 0x4000_0000;
48	
49	/// Size of the user-space device window: 16 MiB, i.e. 4096 pages. TTY uses one;
50	/// the rest is headroom for Phase 6's virtio-mmio register pages.
51	pub const USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE: u64 = 0x0100_0000;
52	
53	/// VA at which the kernel pre-maps the PL011 UART's MMIO page into the TTY
54	/// driver's address space (slice 5.3, decision D1). Page 0 of the window.
55	///
56	/// The mapping is installed once, at boot, by
57	/// `arch::aarch64::userland::load_boot_server` — TTY is a boot server with no
58	/// way to ask for it (there is no `VMCTL_MAP_PHYS`; D1 deferred VM-mediated
59	/// device mapping to Phase 6), so this is a bring-up step exactly like the
60	/// server stack page.
61	pub const TTY_UART_VA: u64 = USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE;
62	
63	/// Size of one L1 slot in the 4 KiB-granule, 4-level, 48-bit-VA walk this
64	/// kernel uses: 512 L2 entries × 512 L3 entries × 4 KiB = 1 GiB.
65	const L1_SLOT_SIZE: u64 = 1 << 30;
66	
67	// The window must start on an L1-slot boundary and fit inside one slot, so the
68	// whole device window costs a single L1 entry and can never share an L2 subtree
69	// with an ordinary mapping.
70	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE.is_multiple_of(L1_SLOT_SIZE));
71	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE <= L1_SLOT_SIZE);
72	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE > 0);
73	
74	// The window must lie inside the user VA range, or `map_page_in`'s `check_va`
75	// would reject every page of it with `MapError::OutOfRange`.
76	const _: () = assert!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE <= USER_VA_TOP);
77	
78	// Every device VA must be page-aligned (a mapping granule) and lie wholly
79	// inside the window.
80	const _: () = assert!(TTY_UART_VA.is_multiple_of(USER_PAGE_SIZE));
81	const _: () = assert!(TTY_UART_VA >= USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE);
82	const _: () =
83	    assert!(TTY_UART_VA + USER_PAGE_SIZE <= USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE);
84	
85	#[cfg(test)]
86	mod tests {
87	    use super::*;
88	
89	    #[test]
90	    fn the_window_is_one_l1_slot_at_one_gib() {
91	        assert_eq!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE, 0x4000_0000);
92	        assert_eq!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE, L1_SLOT_SIZE);
93	        assert_eq!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE, 16 * 1024 * 1024);
94	        // 4096 pages of headroom for Phase 6's virtio-mmio register pages.
95	        assert_eq!(USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE / USER_PAGE_SIZE, 4096);
96	    }
97	
98	    #[test]
99	    fn the_tty_uart_page_is_page_zero_of_the_window() {
100	        assert_eq!(TTY_UART_VA, USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE);
101	        assert_eq!(TTY_UART_VA % USER_PAGE_SIZE, 0);
102	        let window_end = USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE + USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_SIZE;
103	        assert!(TTY_UART_VA + USER_PAGE_SIZE <= window_end);
104	    }
105	
106	    #[test]
107	    fn the_window_clears_every_occupied_user_va() {
108	        // Mirrors the table in the module docs. These are the highest VAs any
109	        // process occupies today (VM's mmap arena base is the top one); the
110	        // window must sit above all of them. The arena is bump-only and grows,
111	        // which is why `servers/vm/src/region.rs` caps it at the window base
112	        // rather than trusting this gap alone.

114	            0x0010_0000_u64, // server / init / worker ELF base
115	            0x0020_0000,     // SERVER_STACK_VA
116	            0x0043_0000,     // stub D code
117	            0x0083_0000,     // stub D stack
118	            0x0100_0000,     // region::HEAP_BASE
119	            0x0200_0000,     // region::MMAP_BASE
120	        ] {
121	            assert!(
122	                occupied < USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE,
123	                "{occupied:#x} collides with the device window"
124	            );
125	        }
126	    }
127	
128	    #[test]
129	    fn the_window_fits_the_user_va_range() {
130	        // `map_page_in`'s `check_va` rejects any VA at or above `USER_VA_TOP`, so

132	        // `MapError::OutOfRange`. (`min` rather than `<`: an all-constant `assert!`

136	        assert_eq!(

138	            end,
139	            "the window runs past USER_VA_TOP"

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! DS (Data Store) client glue used by the SEF init path.
4	//!
5	//! Every server publishes its own endpoint to DS at startup (slice 4.2) so the
6	//! others can look it up by name. The marshaling is trivial and identical for
7	//! all servers, so it lives here rather than being copied into each server's
8	//! `init_fresh` callback. DS itself is the one exception: it seeds its own entry
9	//! in-process (a SENDREC to self would deadlock), so it must *not* call this.
10	//!
11	//! Like [`crate::sef`], this issues an IPC trap, so it is excluded from host
12	//! coverage and verified by the QEMU boot trace.
13	
14	use minixrs_ipc::ipc_sendrec;
15	use minixrs_kernel_shared::Message;
16	use minixrs_kernel_shared::callnr::{DS_PUBLISH, SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN};
17	use minixrs_kernel_shared::com::{DS_PROC_NR, boot_endpoint};
18	use minixrs_kernel_shared::error::OK;
19	
20	/// Publish the caller's own endpoint to DS under `name` (the server's NUL-padded
21	/// name, as learned from `GET_WHOAMI` and passed to the SEF init callback).
22	///
23	/// Builds a key-only `DS_PUBLISH` request — key in payload
24	/// `0..SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN` — and SENDRECs it to DS. The endpoint to register
25	/// is *not* sent in the payload: DS records the kernel-stamped `m_source`, so a
26	/// server can only ever publish itself and cannot spoof another's endpoint.
27	/// Returns `OK` on success, the IPC trap's error if the SENDREC failed, or DS's
28	/// negative reply `m_type`. Intended to be the body of a server's `init_fresh`
29	/// callback.
30	///
31	/// Ordering note: the SENDREC blocks the caller until DS is in its receive loop
32	/// and replies. That is safe at boot — DS's own init does no IPC, so DS reaches
33	/// its loop and never SENDRECs back to a publisher during its own init (no
34	/// cycle).
35	pub fn sef_publish_to_ds(name: &[u8; SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN]) -> i32 {
36	    let mut msg = Message {
37	        m_source: 0,
38	        m_type: DS_PUBLISH,
39	        payload: [0u8; 96],
40	    };
41	    msg.payload[0..SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN].copy_from_slice(name);
42	
43	    let trap_rc = ipc_sendrec(boot_endpoint(DS_PROC_NR), &mut msg);
44	    if trap_rc != OK {
45	        return trap_rc;
46	    }
47	    msg.m_type
48	}

3	// Assembles the per-arch entry path and exception vectors into the kernel.
4	//
5	// .S files go through clang (cross-targeted at the kernel triple) and the
6	// resulting .o files are passed straight to the linker via cargo:rustc-link-arg.
7	// We deliberately *avoid* the cc crate's static-library packaging because the
8	// linker's archive member resolution wouldn't pull in `_start` (it's only
9	// referenced via the linker-script `ENTRY` directive, not from any Rust
10	// symbol). Direct .o linkage sidesteps that, and it also dodges the

17	    // The kernel is bare-metal only. It used to collapse to a no-op `main` on
18	    // host targets so `cargo check --workspace` stayed green, at the cost of
19	    // hiding every module behind `#[cfg(target_os = "none")]` — and therefore
20	    // from every lint gate.
21	    //
22	    // `forced-target` in Cargo.toml now pins this package to
23	    // aarch64-unknown-none for *every* cargo invocation, so in practice this

140	        ("minixrs-init", workspace.join("userland/init"), 10), // INIT_PROC_NR — PID 1
141	        ("minixrs-worker", workspace.join("userland/worker"), -1), // EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR

144	    let mut modules: Vec<(i32, String, Vec<u8>)> = Vec::with_capacity(servers.len());

# Checked by tools/check-boot-log.sh via `grep -aF` (the log interleaves raw

# nr= values are fixed boot-table slots (kernel-shared/src/com.rs).

# Kernel banner (kernel/src/main.rs)

# Address-space bring-up: 7 servers + init (arch/aarch64/userland.rs)
[as] vm nr=7 ttbr0_pa=
[as] ds nr=5 ttbr0_pa=
[as] vfs nr=1 ttbr0_pa=
[as] sched nr=9 ttbr0_pa=
[as] rs nr=2 ttbr0_pa=
[as] pm nr=0 ttbr0_pa=
[as] init nr=10 ttbr0_pa=

# ...plus the 4 boot stubs (11 [as] lines total)
[as] stub A nr=11 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub B nr=12 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub C nr=13 ttbr0_pa=
[as] stub D nr=14 ttbr0_pa=

# init's fork/exec/wait cycle (head-carved kernel traces; slot 15 is the
# fork-pool base, recycled every cycle; exec renames the child to "worker")
[ksys SYS_FORK] parent=i nr=10 child_nr=15
[ksys SYS_EXEC] target=15 name=worker entry=
[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=w nr=15 freed=

# Stub D's designed SIGSEGV chain: page fault -> VM -> SYS_KILL sig=11 -> PM
# tears the stub down with SYS_EXIT
[pf] proc=D far=
[ksys SYS_KILL] target=D nr=14 sig=11 -> pm
[ksys SYS_EXIT] target=D nr=14 freed=

# RS's periodic kernel alarm: assert only the FIRST fire (always inside the
# head carve-out) -- timing-robust under slow CI TCG, unlike a fire count
[alarm 1] owner=r nr=2 at=

# Slice 5.1: stub A's one-shot bad-pointer probes. Each returns EFAULT instead
# of taking an EL1 data abort (which the forbidden list catches as a panic).
# Between them they cover every arm of the copy engine: probe 1 is a fully
# unmapped page, probe 2 straddles A's stack page into the unmapped one above
# it, probe 3 fails in the deferred MF_DELIVERMSG flush and lands EFAULT in A's
# parked x0, and probe 4 names A's *mapped but read-only* code page -- the only
# check on that path is the copy engine's own Prot::writable test, since the
# kernel writes through the HHDM alias where EL0 permission bits do not apply.
# call=1 is SEND; nr=11 is stub A. These lines are unsampled, so unlike
# `[ipc N]` they cannot drift with IPC ordering.
[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x900000
[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=0x800ff8
[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x900000
[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=0x400000

# Slice 5.1: SYS_DIAGCTL is real -- every SEF server announces itself from EL0
# through the kernel debug channel. The name prefix comes from the kernel's own
# proc slot, not the payload, so these lines cannot be spoofed. Assert two of
# the six: vm is the first server packed in the MXBI archive, pm the last, so
# together they bracket the whole roster.
[diag vm] sef ready
[diag pm] sef ready

# Slice 5.2: the grant engine, end to end. VFS direct-grants PM a 64-byte
# read-only buffer and hands the id over in a PM_GRANT_TEST message; PM reads it
# through the grant, then reads the *same* bytes again with the ungranted
# SYS_COPY and compares. `match=1` is the whole point — it proves the grant path
# moved the right bytes, not merely some bytes. Registration is per-granter, so
# both VFS (proc=1) and PM (proc=0) appear; assert VFS's, which is the one the
# demo's grant is served from.
[ksys SYS_SETGRANT] proc=1 entries=
[ksys SYS_SAFECOPY] granter=
[ksys SYS_COPY] src=
[diag pm] grant.test ok
[diag pm] copy ok match=1

# ...and the magic (third-party) arm: PM grants *itself* access to init's text
# page and safecopies out of init's address space, a process that granted
# nothing. Only the length is asserted — the bytes are init's instruction
# encodings and change whenever init is rebuilt. Without this line the magic
# path would be dead code until slice 5.5.
[diag pm] magic ok

# Slice 5.2: the copies that must be REFUSED. Seven safecopies, each valid in
# every respect but one. Five are EPERM from `verify_grant` — wrong grantee,
# wrong access, stale sequence, out-of-range index, past the end of the granted

# the marker disappears. (The `CPF_INDIRECT` and magic-`SYS_PROC` arms are not
# probed; see `grant_denials` in servers/pm for why neither is reachable yet.)
[diag pm] grant.deny ok

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slice 5.3: the TTY console driver and the CDEV band.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The driver announces itself on the kernel debug channel, exactly like the six
# SEF servers. Distinct from the console banner below: this one proves TTY reached
# `sef_startup`, before it has touched any hardware.
[diag tty] sef ready

# The kernel pre-maps the PL011's MMIO page into TTY's address space with Device
# attributes (there is no VMCTL_MAP_PHYS -- D1 deferred VM-mediated device mapping
# to Phase 6, so this is a bring-up step like the stack page). va/pa are fixed
# constants (uspace::TTY_UART_VA, uart::PL011_PHYS_BASE) so both are asserted; the
# attr_idx is NOT, because which MAIR index encodes a Device type depends on what
# the bootloader programmed. Delete this pre-map, or weaken it to a non-writable
# Prot, and TTY's first register store takes an EL0 data abort -- which the
# forbidden list catches.
[devmap] tty va=0x40000000 pa=0x9000000 attr_idx=

# TTY never exits, so `teardown_addrspace`'s device arm would be untested code on a
# live landmine: a missing `prot.device` guard makes `free_frame` panic on the
# UART's PA. `userland::device_teardown_selftest` therefore builds one throwaway
# address space holding exactly one device leaf and tears it down at boot. Both
# counts are asserted -- freed=0 proves the leaf was NOT freed, devs=1 proves it
# was actually seen (a guard that skipped every leaf would give freed=0 devs=0).
# Unconditional, so the --no-default-features boot covers it too.
[devmap] selftest ok freed=0 devs=1

# attributes (there is no VMCTL_MAP_PHYS -- D1 deferred VM-mediated device mapping
# to Phase 6, so this is a bring-up step like the stack page). va/pa are fixed
# constants (uspace::TTY_UART_VA, uart::PL011_PHYS_BASE) so both are asserted; the
# attr_idx is NOT, because which MAIR index already encodes a Device type depends on
# what the bootloader programmed. Delete this pre-map, or weaken it to a
# non-writable Prot, and TTY's first register store takes an EL0 data abort -- which
# the forbidden list catches.
[devmap] tty va=0x40000000 pa=0x9000000 attr_idx=

# TTY never exits, so `teardown_addrspace`'s device arm would be untested code on a
# live landmine: a missing `prot.device` guard makes `free_frame` panic on the
# UART's PA. `userland::device_teardown_selftest` therefore builds one throwaway
# address space holding exactly one device leaf and tears it down at boot. Both
# counts are asserted -- freed=0 proves the leaf was NOT freed, devs=1 proves it was
# actually seen (a guard that skipped every leaf would give freed=0 devs=0).
# Unconditional, so the --no-default-features boot covers it too.
[devmap] selftest ok freed=0 devs=1

# The milestone. Every other line in this log carries a kernel trace prefix
# ([as] / [ipc] / [ksys] / [diag] / [pf] / [devmap]); this one was composed at EL0
# and reached the wire through a user-space store to a device register.
minix.rs console: tty online (EL0)

# Slice 5.3: VFS drives the console over CDEV_WRITE. It resolves TTY through DS
# rather than hard-coding boot_endpoint(TTY_PROC_NR) -- what a real client does. The
# lookup is not deterministic by construction (it works because build.rs packs tty
# before vfs), so a failed lookup falls back to the boot endpoint and emits
# `cdev.ds FAIL` instead: the demo still runs, and *this* marker disappears, so an
# ordering regression turns CI red specifically rather than silently passing.
[diag vfs] cdev.ds ok ep=

# A real write: a read-only direct grant over VFS's banner, and a reply compared
# against the granted length. `match=1` rather than the length itself -- self-
# checking, and independent of the banner text. A driver replying OK instead of the
# byte count gives match=0.
[diag vfs] cdev.write ok match=1

# The short-write contract: VFS asks for CDEV_MAX_IO + 8 bytes and must get exactly
# CDEV_MAX_IO back. That is what lets a driver stage through a fixed buffer with no
# allocator, and it is the difference between "write returns a count" and "write
# returns success". Change the clamp and this number changes with it.
[diag vfs] cdev.short ok n=256

# ...and the two requests that must be REFUSED, each valid in every respect but
# one: minor 7 with a perfectly good grant (ENXIO, from TTY's own minor check), and
# a grant issued to PM rather than TTY (EPERM, from the kernel's `who_to` check --
# the property that makes a grant id safe to pass around at all). Remove either
# check and that request succeeds, so this line becomes `cdev.deny FAIL <name>`.
[diag vfs] cdev.deny ok n=2

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! Userland bootstrap: per-process address spaces with 8-bit ARMv8 ASIDs.
4	//!
5	//! Everything the kernel starts at EL0 is built here. Two shapes:
6	//!
7	//!   - **Boot servers and init**, loaded from the MXBI archive by
8	//!     [`load_boot_server`] — an ELF load plus one stack page. Slice 4.7
9	//!     factored the address-space half out as [`load_exec_image`], which
10	//!     `system::do_exec` reuses to re-image a live proc.
11	//!   - **Demo stubs A–D** (`boot-stubs` feature, default on), built by
12	//!     [`build_stub`] from raw blobs in `user_stub.S` — one code page, one
13	//!     stack page. They are the standing regression battery for the IPC
14	//!     primitives, SCHED delegation, VM page faults, and (as of slice 5.1)
15	//!     the fault-safe user copy; init and worker exercise none of that.
16	//!
17	//! Either way the proc gets its own [`AddrSpace`], frames come from
18	//! [`crate::mm`], contents are written through the HHDM
19	//! (`mm::phys_to_hhdm`) rather than the not-yet-active TTBR0, and the
20	//! resulting `(ttbr0_pa, asid)` is stored on the proc slot. The scheduler
21	//! ([`crate::proc::sched::schedule_next`]) installs that TTBR0 on every
22	//! EL1 → EL0 transition.
23	//!
24	//! The tree is owned by the proc slot from then on, not by an `AddrSpace`
25	//! value — hence the `mem::forget` at the end of each builder. Teardown goes
26	//! through `system::do_exit`, which frees leaf frames before the tables.
27	//!
28	//! No page is ever shared between stubs: each maps its own frame at its own
29	//! VA, so there is no kernel-global user mapping to reason about.

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
2	// Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
3	//! minix.rs TTY driver — the console, TX only (slice 5.3, decision D1).
4	//!
5	//! The first user-space *driver* in minix.rs, and the first EL0-originated text on
6	//! the serial line. Everything before it either came from the kernel's own PL011
7	//! writer or rode the `SYS_DIAGCTL` debug channel — which is deliberately a debug
8	//! channel, not stdio.
9	//!
10	//! TTY owns the PL011 and serves [`CDEV_WRITE`]. A client grants it a read-only
11	//! view of a buffer, sends the grant id, and TTY pulls the bytes across with
12	//! `SYS_SAFECOPY` before transmitting them. Slice 5.4 puts VFS's fd 1 and 2 on top
13	//! of this; slice 5.6's musl `printf` rides the same rails.
14	//!
15	//! Built as a freestanding aarch64 ELF (`drivers/tty/user.ld`, a byte copy of the
16	//! servers'), packed into the MXBI archive by `kernel/build.rs`, and loaded into
17	//! its own address space at boot — plus one extra page the other boot processes do
18	//! not get: the UART's MMIO registers at `TTY_UART_VA`, pre-mapped by the kernel
19	//! with Device attributes. See `pl011.rs`.
20	//!
21	//! ## Three things that differ from a server
22	//!
23	//! **An unknown `m_type` gets a reply, not a drop.** DS silently drops one, which
24	//! is fine when nothing SENDRECs it in anger — but a driver's clients *all*
25	//! SENDREC, and a dropped request blocks the caller forever. Every path out of the
26	//! dispatch below replies.
27	//!
28	//! **The granter comes from `m_source`.** TTY holds `SYS_SAFECOPY`; its clients do
29	//! not. A granter field in the payload would let any client aim a privileged
30	//! cross-address-space copy at a third party's memory through TTY. `cdev.rs` has no
31	//! way to express one.
32	//!
33	//! **A negative `SYS_SAFECOPY` result is relayed verbatim.** `EPERM` ("your grant
34	//! does not authorize this") and `EFAULT` ("your buffer is not mapped") are
35	//! different bugs on the client's side, and collapsing them to one errno would hide
36	//! which.

38	// Freestanding for the real (bare-metal) build, but a normal host binary under
39	// `cargo test` so `cdev`'s logic gets host-runnable unit tests. The test harness
40	// needs `std` and its own entry point, so `no_std`/`no_main` and the `_start` shim
41	// below are all gated to `not(test)`.

43	#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_main)]

56	/// usable from EL0.
57	///
58	/// This line is the slice's milestone, and it is recognizable in the boot log for a
59	/// specific reason: it carries **no kernel trace prefix**. Every other line in the
60	/// log is `[as]`, `[ipc]`, `[ksys …]`, `[diag …]` — kernel-formatted. This one was
61	/// composed at EL0 and reached the wire through a user-space store to a device
62	/// register.
63	const BANNER: &str = "minix.rs console: tty online (EL0)\n";
64	
65	/// ELF entry point. The kernel primes `SP_EL0` before `eret`, so `_start` can dive
66	/// straight into Rust without setting up a stack itself.
67	// Gate the whole shim to `not(test)`: under `cargo test` the crate links as a
68	// normal host executable, and an exported `_start` would collide with the C
69	// runtime's. `.text._start` is an ELF section name, gated to the bare-metal target

71	#[cfg(not(test))]
72	#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
73	#[cfg_attr(target_os = "none", unsafe(link_section = ".text._start"))]
74	pub extern "C" fn _start() -> ! {
75	    main()
76	}
77	
78	// Only `_start` calls `main`; under `cargo test` `_start` is gone, so `main` (and

81	fn main() -> ! {
82	    let sef = sef_startup(SefConfig {
83	        init_fresh: Some(tty_init),

85	    })

88	        // learned its own endpoint, so it cannot even announce the failure.
89	        loop {
